scope: Main album shelf alignment on distant selection/reordering and rapid re-selection, preserving nearby motion, original artwork and lazy preview/cache ownership.

findings.before: The focused stage already jumped for distant selection, but the small cover shelf always animated its full distance. A controlled 201-album selection from 0 to 160 mounted intermediate covers: strip IDs 27-31, 52-57, 75-79, 93-98 and more; the grid also mounted intermediate IDs. A refreshed/reordered selected album can also move to a distant index.
findings.change: Animate only within 1.5 scroll viewports. Jump directly for distant alignment. Existing layout alignment stays immediate, and fixed list/grid extents and lazy builders are unchanged.
findings.verified: Both strip and grid now show album 160 immediately without mounting IDs 20-130 during subsequent frames, retain fewer than 20 mounted cover previews in the fixture, and still animate intermediate offsets for nearby selection.

findings.before: Selecting a nearby album and returning to album 0 before the first animation tick left the old scroll activity running, because the new alignment returned early at distance <1. The strip ended at offset 112 while album 0 was selected; the grid case also failed.
findings.change: If alignment is already at the requested position but a scroll activity is still running, jump to the target to stop that obsolete activity before returning.
findings.verified: Both strip and grid stay at offset 0 after rapid return, leave the selected album visible and stop the scroll activity. Teardown leaves no transient callbacks.

baseline.classification: Intentional pre-fix reproduction; the four failing cases cover far selection and rapid return for strip/grid. Nearby/reduced-motion cases passed before and after.

intermediate_related.classification: The shared unit_test_assets directory existed but lacked AssetManifest.bin and Poppins-Regular.otf. --no-test-assets could not reuse the absent bundle. Two artwork tests and one font setup failed; all eight new controlled cases passed. No production code was changed for the missing test assets.

final_related.asset_handling: Allowed Flutter to regenerate only the test asset bundle for the final run; no app build or device execution.

verification.scoped_git_diff_check: passed; additionally checked source/test trailing whitespace and exact delta against the pre-run snapshot
verification.resources: Free disk rechecked before tests (~3.9 GiB); no other Flutter test process was observed at the prelaunch checks. Each agent-owned test process ran serially. No other process or user/shared cache was stopped or removed.
verification.external_effects: No app build/device run, deployment, operational database access or customer data mutation.

checked: No widget tree, layout spacing, text, title, category, sort/filter, item key, image decode budget or cache implementation was changed.
The only production delta is the distance gate plus cancellation of an obsolete scroll activity; no extra queue, listener, timer, cache or controller was added.
Existing reduced-motion, TickerMode and mounted/controller attachment checks remain in place.

Existing main/collection completion criteria, queued large-document work, memory-pressure cleanup, photo preparation/capture, reader navigation, rotation, selection retention after refresh and cover-opening tests pass.
New teardown assertions verify no remaining transient frame callback; source review confirms the existing owned ScrollController disposal is unchanged.
Shared workspace changes and all snapshot-protected sources were preserved.

next_candidates: Review editor material/photo picker async completion after dismissal, account changes and rapid tool switching against the latest completed records.
Continue main album queued cover/progress visibility and owner checks if a new controlled failure appears; do not repeat the completed shelf/reader alignment fixes.
Before reusing --no-test-assets, verify AssetManifest.bin and required fixture fonts actually exist; check free disk and active tests before compilation.

limits: No physical-device FPS, frame-time, peak process memory or heap snapshot was measured. Skipped intermediate widget construction is proven; numerical FPS or MB savings and a whole-app absence of leaks are not claimed.

The controlled 201-album fixtures use small layer-free cover documents and count mounted cover widgets, not network requests or native photo allocations. Existing real-artwork/reader fixtures supply the related regressions.
Already-started image/worker operations remain governed by their existing shared visibility/disposal gates; this change does not cancel network transport or replace cache policies.
